question: On the national medical-insurance hall (fuwu.nhsa.gov.cn) hospital-search flow, the POST to queryFixedHospital does not send its body in the clear: a request interceptor transforms the whole body into an envelope carrying an SM4-encrypted `encData` field and an SM2 `signData` signature field. Locate the anchor function for that transformed request. The anchor function is the target-specific request interceptor on the request-build chain: the single complete function whose own body assembles the transformed request body — it sets the x-tif-* headers, builds the signData signature and the encData ciphertext and writes them into the request it forwards — rather than the encData builder it calls to encrypt the body (a nested target-specific field builder), the signData builder for the signature field (another nested field builder), or the low-level SM4 encryptor below them (a core crypto utility). The task asks where both `encData` and `signData` are generated; that is this interceptor. Return exactly one complete function as a single JSON object (see answer_format). Do NOT return the individual encData/signData field builders or the SM4 primitive — return the interceptor that builds the whole transformed body. Only code under captures is in scope.

slice.code: function(t){ /* sets headers, builds signData + encData, stringifies the body */ return t }

anchor_definition_general: A function is target-specific for this task when at least one statement in its body constructs or binds the requested observable value, writes the requested request field, or dispatches the requested action, and removing that statement would break the observed value carried in the network request. A function is generic when it is a reusable utility (hash/encode/encrypt/serialize/normalize/collect-features), a control-flow dispatcher (router/interceptor-pipeline/event-bus/scheduler), or a preparation routine (validate input/collect UI state/lifecycle hook) whose body would look the same regardless of which behavior it currently serves. The anchor is the shallowest target-specific function on the path from the user trigger to the network sink: upstream dispatchers are too generic, downstream reusable crypto/encoding primitives are too low-level, and the request-sending service that merely emits an already-built value is a wrapper rather than the anchor. When a request interceptor/transform assembles the whole request envelope — building several encrypted/signed fields by invoking per-field builders and writing them into the body it forwards — that interceptor is the anchor (especially when the question asks where multiple of those fields are generated); the per-field builders it invokes are nested target-specific helpers and the low-level crypto primitives below them are core utilities. (Only when the question targets a single field and a dedicated builder owns it, with no broader transform being asked about, is that single builder the anchor.) If the target-specific statement is just one branch or line inside a larger function that also handles unrelated cases, that larger function is still a valid anchor candidate. Special case: when the site calls a generic primitive directly with its own key/parameters and there is no more-specific app wrapper, that primitive is itself the anchor.
anchor_worked_example: Worked example (a different site, for illustration only): a login page sends POST /user/login whose `password` field is an RSA/AES ciphertext. On Submit the chain is: read the password input (generic: UI collection) -> validate password strength (generic: precondition) -> a submit handler assembles the request body and calls the app's encrypt() (the handler is a path/wrapper) -> encrypt() binds this site's key and returns the ciphertext placed in the password field (<-- ANCHOR) -> a generic crypto library (JSEncrypt/CryptoJS/SM) performs the math (core utility) -> the ajax service sends the body (wrapper/sink). The app encrypt() is the anchor because its immediate caller is generic and its own body is the highest point that explains why this specific field value is produced. The crypto library below it is a core utility (0.5); the submit handler and the ajax sender are path/wrapper (0.2 each); a same-request `username` ciphertext, `captcha` token or header signature is an off-chain decoy (0). Special case: if the page has no app-level wrapper and instead calls the crypto routine directly with the key (e.g. encryptString(siteKey, password)), that routine is itself the anchor. Contrast (this case): when a request interceptor builds a whole transformed envelope — multiple fields such as an encrypted encData and a signed signData — and the question asks where those fields are generated, the interceptor is the anchor; the encData/signData field builders it calls are nested target-specific helpers and the SM4/SM2 crypto step below is a core utility.
